features.name: Fief 'heartbeat' problems (steward summons to solve local crises)
features.summary: Every few days one of the player's fiefs may develop a problem (rats, flood, curse/witch, clan blood-feud, horse thieves, wolves, refugees, fire, poisoned wells, captured heretic, cult spies, shrine dispute, disease, mercenaries asking for work, thieves, castle repairs, deserters, trade-route petitions). A messenger summons the player; he can ride there and choose one of four responses, pay 500 denars to have it handled remotely, or ignore it and lose honour, morale and village relation.
features.mechanics: strig:20 (every 96h, 50% chance) picks a random center led by the player (get_number_of_hero_centers / troop_get_leaded_center_with_index), stores a problem id 1-13 in party slot 296 and raises menu_heartbeat_quest via add_notification_menu (or just a log line if $notif_village_help=1). menu:heartbeat_quest offers accept / pay 500 (clears slot 296) / decline (-1 honour, -5 party morale, -5 center relation, clears slot). When the player talks to the elder or seneschal of that fief, dlg:1065 (start state) fires if slot 296>=1, shows a random intro string, dlg:1066-1067 state the problem (str_heartbeat_problem_statement_N + variants a-d) and dlg:1068-1071 offer four responses that call pop3_heartbeat_resolve(choice, problem). The 2056-statement resolver rolls success against the player's skill 7 and the steward's skills 15/22/7/8 plus bonuses from built improvements it reads up front (party slots 250 herbalist, 257 hunting lodge, 259 sheriff, 265 church, 267 fire brigade, 270 shrine, 274 training grounds, 276 hospital, 278 cathedral, 283 well cleaners, 286 thieves guild, 287 town crier, 288 civic patrols, 289 knighthood chapter) and applies prosperity, gold, relation (center/faction/troop), renown, honour and morale changes, sometimes spawning parties (looters, heretics, mercenaries).

features.name: Expanded fief buildings with damage, auto-repair and AI lord construction
features.summary: Villages, castles and towns each get their own long list of buildings (about 38 in total: mine and prospecting, herbalist, market, skilled craftsmen, manor, fish pond, school, watch tower, messenger post, prison tower, winery, hunting lodge, foresters, sheriff, shrine, blacksmith, hospital, university, thieves guild, training grounds, church, cathedral, monastery, chapel, crop rotation, court system, warehouse, guilds, lamplighters, well cleaners, street sweepers, building inspectors, renderers, tax office, fire brigade, town crier, civic patrols, improved roads, sanitation). Buildings add base income and prosperity, can be damaged by war and are repaired over time; AI lords also spend their own wealth building in their fiefs.
features.mechanics: get_improvement_details (243 stmts vs Native 32) maps party slots 250-289 to name/description/cost; ranges are per center type (village 250-272, castle 260-275, town 262-288). Slot value 1 = built and working, 2..9 = damaged level. strig:76 (12h) completes construction from Native slots 124/125 (improvement in progress / finish hour) and calls center_base_income_change(center, slot, 1) which adds the building's income/prosperity effect (221 stmts, also called when buildings are damaged in game_event_simulate_battle, village_set_state, peace/truce dialogs). auto_repair_buildings (strig:123, ~weekly) walks damaged buildings: AI fiefs repair by the steward/lord engineering skill (skill 8) per week; player fiefs repair only if Skilled Craftsmen (slot 268) is built and the player can afford 200 x skill denars. random_build_buildings (strig:124, every ~20 days) lets non-player lords (troop slot 11 = wealth) roll to build a missing building, paying 1/5 of the cost. Mines (slot 269) take a prospecting result (get_mineral_value) and give direct income; can be closed by steward dialog (dlg:2294-2296).

features.name: Passive training of lord parties and garrisons (with garrison sorting)
features.summary: Every two days AI lords' parties and all non-player garrisons gain free upgrade XP (more on easy campaign AI, less on hard); player fiefs train their garrisons according to the steward's trainer skill and training grounds. Garrisons are re-sorted so the best troops sit at the top of the stack list.

features.name: Joinable knighthood orders with rank points, order quests and expulsion
features.summary: The player can petition a knighthood order at its chapterhouse, pass a test of arms in the arena against the order's champion, and become a member. Order work (bounty hunting, winning a tournament in the order's name, a 'challenge' of many victories with lent order troops, settling a rivalry with another order) earns rank points; seven rank tiers unlock titles, order armour sets and recruitment of the order's knights. Acting against the order strips membership.
features.mechanics: Membership is stored on the player as troop slot 162 (order leader/troop whose faction is the order). Order quest givers (hall_order_guard_talk -> order_choose_quest dlg:3879-3884) issue qst_order_bounty / qst_order_tournament / order challenge / qst_order_rivalry; rewards (dlg:3891, 3898, 3904, 3912) give XP, renown, honour, faction relation and 6-8+ rank points (bounty scales by value killed). Promotions dlg:3796/3811; expulsion dlg:3799; resignation dlg:3867/3871; order books can be sold for rank (dlg:3842/3844); armour sets bought via buy_order_armour_set.

Their engineering, trade, trainer and other skills drive building repair and AI construction, garrison training, heartbeat-crisis outcomes and income. The lord can hold a paid 'training session' (a few hours of waiting, 150 denars per hour) that raises the steward's skills up to the best in the player's party. The steward is also the hub for feasts, tournaments, gossip, mine closing and the war room.

Gated by $g_option_formations (prsnt_mod_options) and $g_disciplined_faction (see pop.disciplined_faction_ai_gate).

features.name: Only disciplined armies use formation AI; rabble fights as a mob
features.summary: Before a battle PoP decides whether the enemy is a 'disciplined' force. Bandits, outlaws, rebel peasants, tribal raiders, militia and similar rabble fight without formations or field tactics, while kingdoms, orders and named warlords use the full formation AI. Formation AI and rout behaviour are also switchable in mod options.
features.mechanics: set_disciplined_faction (35 stmts; called from 7 menus and 4 mission triggers) sets $g_disciplined_faction = 1, then 0 if the encountered party or its ally ($g_encountered_party / $g_encountered_party_2) belongs to fac_outlaws, fac_red_brotherhood, fac_rebel_peasants, fac_mystmountain, fac_dshar_raiders, fac_militia, fac_mountain_bandits, fac_forest_bandits or fac_singalians AND its template is not a signature warlord (not between pt_wolfbode and pt_refugees). battle_tactic_init_aux / battle_tactic_apply_aux, mst_lead_charge t28-t63 and castle sally triggers test $g_disciplined_faction (and $g_option_formations) before running formation/field-tactics code. $g_option_routing gates the rout trigger mst:lead_charge/t32 (decide_run_away_or_not every 3s).

features.name: Walk among and drill your army from the camp menu
features.summary: From the camp menu the player can 'walk around and review your soldiers': the whole party is spawned in a random field scene where the player can inspect troops and practise formation orders without a battle.
features.mechanics: menu:camp/opt:camp_action_1 sets jump mission mst_camp_review_soldiers, counts fit troops (party_count_fit_for_battle) and calls setup_random_scene, then change_screen_mission. The mission template carries the same formation/field-tactics triggers as lead_charge (t10-t30: cf_formation, field_tactics) plus a tab-to-leave trigger (t0).

features.name: Procedural rumours and gossip with per-NPC cooldowns
features.summary: Tavernkeepers, travellers, ransom brokers, merchants and the player's steward tell randomly assembled rumours (who told it, what it is about, main-story hints), or say they have nothing new if asked again too soon. A mod option sets how often rumours refresh.
features.mechanics: random_rumor_talk(kind, npc) (966 stmts) checks troop slot 157 (last rumour day) + $g_rumor_interval against the current day; if on cooldown builds a 'no news' line from 9 variants; otherwise picks a topic via rumor_topic (206 stmts) and a source via rumor_who_from (650 stmts), seeded by weekly $event_rand_* (update_event_rand), occasionally main_scenario_conversation_overheard, and stores the new day in slot 157. Entry: dlg:2695 tavernkeeper, dlg:2855 traveller, dlg:2778 ransom broker, dlg:3724 merchant, dlg:2287 steward gossip.

features.name: Per-fief base income with income and construction reports
features.summary: Every center has a 'base income' value (raised by buildings, lowered by damage and raids) that feeds its weekly wealth, and the Reports menu adds a fief income report (base income and prosperity of each of the player's fiefs, plus a list of fiefs with pending heartbeat crises) and a construction report (what is being built where and how many days remain).
features.mechanics: Party slot 290 holds base income: initialised in pop2_location_improvements, changed by center_base_income_change (building completed/damaged/repaired, raids, peace deals) and a steward's lavish tournament (dlg:2307). strig:26 (weekly) adds 1000 + prosperity x 14 + base income x 4 (x1.3 in five capital towns) minus garrison wage (x3/4 when the player's spouse/minister owns it) to Native town wealth (slot 49) for non-player centers. menu:reports/opt:view_center_income_report -> menu:center_income_report lists player fiefs with slot 290 and slot 50 prosperity text; option lists fiefs with party slot 296 set; menu:center_construction_report reads Native slots 124/125 and get_improvement_details to print 'building X, N days left'. Steward/elder dialogs dlg:2431 / dlg:3407 report the same numbers in person.
